children: Indian shares opened higher on Wednesday, with the benchmarks rebounding after the Nifty 50 closed at a five-month low in the previous session, although higher crude prices and caution ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy decision capped gains.
rose 0.51% to 23,240.6, while the BSE Sensex added 0.51% to 74,390.57, as of 9:21 a.m. IST.
Both the benchmarks are in oversold territory, so a technical bounce cannot be ruled out from current levels, two traders said.
However, the overall sentiment remains subdued due to elevated crude oil prices, heightened activity in the primary market and expectations of a likely rate hike by the Fed later in the day.
All 16 major sectors logged gains. The broader small-caps
rose between 2.7% and 5% after the 0.4% merchant discount rate (MDR) hike on select person-to-merchant transactions above 2,000 rupees from October 15.
, which rose 2.2%, reversed gains to trade 3.6% lower.
